about.title: Tiburon Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Tiburon's mix of hillside walkways, marina-front businesses, and older shopping areas along Tiburon Boulevard and Paradise Drive can create hazards that aren't always obvious until someone gets hurt. Whether the fall happened on a rain-slicked deck near the water, a cracked sidewalk, or a poorly lit stairwell in a private building, California law requires the property owner to have known or reasonably should have known about the danger before they can be held responsible. That's why documenting the scene matters so much here — a wet floor sign that wasn't out, a broken step that had been reported before, or surveillance footage that shows how long a spill sat unattended. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself; we simply connect injured Tiburon residents and visitors with an independent attorney who can evaluate the property owner's notice and negligence, all on a contingency basis, so there's no fee unless the case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Notice and Timing Matter in Your Claim

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew or Should Have Known
items.desc: California premises liability hinges on notice — an attorney can help gather evidence showing the property owner was aware of the hazard, or that it existed long enough that they should have caught it.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Tiburon businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks, so getting a preservation request out quickly can be critical to your case.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Have to Bar Recovery
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still pursue compensation even if you were partly responsible for the fall — your recovery is simply adjusted to reflect your share of fault.

items.question: I fell at a business off Tiburon Boulevard. Do I have a case?
items.answer: It depends on whether the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard that caused your fall and failed to fix or warn about it. An independent attorney can review what happened, look at the maintenance history and any available footage, and let you know whether the facts support a claim.

items.question: How long do I have to file a premises liability claim in California?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit, though claims against a public entity — like a city-owned sidewalk or park — often have a much shorter deadline. It's worth reaching out sooner rather than later so evidence like video and witness accounts can still be gathered.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for not watching where I was walking?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame for the fall. Your total recovery would just be reduced by whatever percentage of fault is assigned to you.
